verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti;
verses.english: “A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṁ anādhāraṁ suppavattiyaṁ hoti, sādhāraṁ duppavattiyaṁ hoti.
verses.english: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.
And what’s the stand for the mind?
It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
This is the stand for the mind.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti;
verses.english: A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṁ anādhāraṁ suppavattiyaṁ hoti, sādhāraṁ duppavattiyaṁ hotī”ti.
verses.english: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.”
